previous_assumption: Two fixed global roles (owner/member) shared across every organization was documented as deliberate ('add custom roles when a real need appears' — see migration 0002's own comment).
correction: That real need appeared: an invited 'member' had zero permissions seeded, ever, with no endpoint or UI to grant any (client-verified live). roles.organization_id is now nullable — NULL is the one built-in global role ('owner', always full access, immutable via the API), a real org id scopes a role and its permissions to exactly one organization. Migration 0027 gives every existing org its own 'member' role and repoints all memberships/invites off the old global one before deleting it; AuthService.signup does the same for every new org going forward. Full create/edit/delete on an organization's own roles via organization.manage; permission codes validated against PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES at save time; moving a member between roles (membership.manage, PATCH /organizations/:id/members/:id) refuses to leave an org with zero active owners. Verified live end-to-end including the exact reported scenario: create a custom role with real permissions, invite straight into it, new account has that access immediately.
